title: Thioredoxin-Interacting Protein-Regulated in Development and DNA Damage-Response 1-Driven Macrophage Senescence Promotes Hypoxia-Induced Pulmonary Hypertension.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Background Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by pulmonary arterial remodeling and right ventricular failure, posing a significant clinical challenge. Although macrophage dysfunction is implicated in PH pathogenesis, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Methods We employed multiomics database analysis, cross-species validation, and functional studies in hypoxia-induced PH models. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion was achieved via bone marrow transplantation in mice. Mechanistic insights were evaluated through protein-binding assays, cellular senescence analyses in bone marrow-derived macrophages, and co-culture experiments with pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells. Results We identified that cellular senescence in pulmonary adventitial macrophages was involved in the pathogenesis of hypoxia-induced PH. Integrated multiomics analysis revealed elevated TXNIP (thioredoxin-interacting protein) expression in perivascular macrophages during hypoxia-induced PH. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion attenuated hypoxia-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling in mice. Mechanistically, TXNIP binds to and stabilizes the REDD1 (regulated in development and DNA damage-response 1) protein, promoting hypoxia-induced senescence in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Conditioned medium from senescent macrophages subsequently enhanced the proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells. Conclusions The TXNIP-REDD1 axis drives hypoxia-induced macrophage senescence, which promotes pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell dysfunction and pulmonary vascular remodeling in hypoxia-induced PH. Targeting the TXNIP-REDD1 pathway may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for hypoxia-induced PH.
ids: title:thioredoxin interacting protein regulated in development and dna damage response 1 driven macrophage senescence promotes hypoxia induced pulmonary hypertension

title: Multiomics Insights Linking Personal Care Products Exposure to Serum Lipid Profiles in Older Adults: The China BAPE Study.
summary: Exposure to four personal care product chemicals (BP‑2, BP‑3, 4‑OHBP, EtP) was linked to altered serum lipid profiles in older adults through a prospective panel of 76 participants with urinary, lipidomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic measurements. Multi‑omics integration indicated convergence on a peroxisome proliferator‑activated receptor‑centered immunometabolic network, with BP‑2 associated with alternative macrophage activation, inflammation, oxidative damage and ECG changes.
abstract: Personal care products (PCPs) are widespread environmental exposures, yet their combined and system-wide effects on serum lipid profiles in the aging population remain poorly understood. This study aimed to comprehensively assess the association between exposure to multiple PCPs and serum lipid profiles in healthy older adults and to explore underlying molecular pathways and biological mechanisms. We conducted a prospective panel study with five monthly follow-up surveys between September 2018 and January 2019 among 76 healthy older adults (60-69 years) in Jinan, China. This study measured urinary concentrations of PCPs, serum lipid markers, and multiomics profiles (transcriptomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics). We employed linear mixed-effects models to analyze exposure-outcome associations and integrated multiomics data with causal inference testing and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis to identify mediating biomolecules and biological mechanisms. Additional analyses examined the relationships of PCP exposures with inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress biomarkers, and electrocardiographic (ECG) parameters to provide functional support for the identified pathways and their associated phenotypic consequences. Four PCPs [Benzophenone-2 (BP-2), Benzophenone-3 (BP-3), 4-Hydroxy benzophenone (4-OHBP), and Ethyl p-Hydroxybenzoate (EtP)] were significantly associated with altered serum lipid profiles. Multiomics analyses suggested their convergence on a PPAR-centered immunometabolic network, with S100 signaling identified as a novel activation pathway. Specifically, BP-2 was associated with patterns consistent with IL-4/IL-13-mediated alternative macrophage activation, while PPAR appeared to be involved in inflammatory polarization and metabolic reprogramming. Cytokine analysis revealed associations between BP-2 and key inflammatory mediators (e.g., IL-1β), oxidative stress assessment linked BP-2 exposure to elevated markers of oxidative damage (e.g., 8-PGF2α), and ECG analysis associated BP-2 exposure with altered cardiac electrophysiology (e.g., QRS duration). These multifaceted findings suggest associations between PCP exposures and serum lipid profiles, and highlight the potential contribution to cardiovascular risk. Our findings provide integrated, multilayered evidence suggesting associations between exposure to PCPs and alterations in serum lipid profiles in older adults, bridging exposure profiles, biomolecular perturbations, and subclinical functional changes. These results serve as a hypothesis-generating theoretical foundation that, pending confirmation in larger studies or experimental validation, advances the understanding of environmental metabolic disruption in aging populations.
ids: title:multiomics insights linking personal care products exposure to serum lipid profiles in older adults the china bape study

title: Endothelial cell-microglia crosstalk mediates heart failure-associated synaptic loss and cognitive impairment in male mice.
summary: Heart failure–induced circulating factors were shown to cause senescence of cerebral endothelial cells, which then secreted SPARC via a MEK/ERK‑MYC pathway, activating microglial Toll‑like receptor 4 and leading to synaptic loss and cognitive decline in male mice. Genetic deletion of endothelial Tgfbr2 or Sparc, or microglial Tlr4, preserved synapses and improved cognition, indicating an endothelial‑microglia axis as a therapeutic target.
abstract: Cognitive impairment affects 30%-80% of patients with heart failure, yet the mechanisms beyond reduced brain blood flow remain poorly defined. Here we show that circulating factors released during heart failure trigger senescence of brain blood-vessel endothelial cells, which in turn drives synaptic loss and cognitive decline through crosstalk between endothelial cells and microglia, the brain's immune cells. Using a pressure-overload model (transverse aortic constriction) combined with plasma transfer in 8-month-old male mice, we found that elevated circulating TGFβ2 acts on endothelial TGFBR2 and induces the secreted protein SPARC via a non-canonical MEK/ERK-MYC pathway. Endothelial SPARC then activates microglial TLR4, promoting neuroinflammation and abnormal engulfment of synapses. Endothelial deletion of Tgfbr2 or Sparc, and microglial deletion of Tlr4, each preserved synapses and improved cognition, and pharmacological Tlr4 inhibition was protective. These findings define an endothelial-microglia signaling axis and a potential therapeutic target in heart failure-associated cognitive impairment.
ids: title:endothelial cell microglia crosstalk mediates heart failure associated synaptic loss and cognitive impairment in male mice

title: Targeting Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell Senescence for Cardiovascular Pharmacology: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a central role in maintaining vascular tone, structural integrity, and adaptive remodeling. With aging and chronic cardiometabolic stress, however, VSMCs undergo senescence driven by telomere attrition, oxidative stress, persistent DNA-damage signaling, and dysregulation of the p53/p21 and p16/Rb pathways. This transition is accompanied by acquisition of a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which promotes inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, calcification and vascular stiffening. Together, these accelerate atherosclerosis, hypertension, aneurysm formation, and related vasculopathies. Growing evidence identifies VSMC senescence as a promising therapeutic entry point for cardiovascular drug discovery. Emerging strategies include senolytics, senomorphics, metabolic modulators, and molecular reprogramming approaches designed to either eliminate senescent cells or attenuate their pathogenic secretome and downstream signaling networks. In this review, the molecular basis of VSMC senescence, its contribution to major vascular disorders, and the therapeutic landscape targeting senescence-associated pathways are discussed, with emphasis on translational opportunities and current barriers to clinical application. A clearer understanding of VSMC senescence may inform the development of mechanism-based interventions to limit vascular dysfunction and age-related cardiovascular disease.
ids: title:targeting vascular smooth muscle cell senescence for cardiovascular pharmacology mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives

title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance. During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination. Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk and may provide complementary information for risk stratification.
ids: title:combined prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance derived myocardial extracellular volume and the fibrosis 4 index in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

title: Exposomic Determinants in Heart Failure Among Older Adults - Mechanistic Links, Clinical Evidence, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Heart failure (HF) in older adults emerges from the interplay between biological aging and the totality of environmental and behavioural exposures conceptualized as the exposome. Traditional cardiovascular risk factors and intrinsic cardiac pathology only partially explain HF burden, as chronic exposures to air pollution, traffic noise, temperature extremes, toxic metals and chemicals, artificial light at night, and adverse social environments, along with low greenness and walkability, substantially influence HF incidence, decompensations, and prognosis in older patients with multiple comorbidities. Recently, epidemiological studies have associated many of the exposomic factors with HF incidence and morbidity. Age‑related impairments of the myocardium and vasculature make them particularly vulnerable to external stressors. Mechanistically, aging, HF, and environmental factors converge on shared pathways including, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammaging, impaired autophagy and proteostasis, genomic and epigenetic alterations, cellular senescence, dysregulated neurohormonal and circadian signalling, and fibrosis with maladaptive remodelling. Through these mechanisms exposome chronically accelerates cardiovascular aging and lowers the threshold for HF onset and progression. This review considers a shift from an organ‑centred view of HF in older adults to a systems‑level, life‑course perspective that explicitly incorporates exposomic determinants, and argues that reducing harmful exposures while promoting green space, physical activity, walkability, and healthy dietary patterns should be integral to HF prevention and management strategies in aging societies.
ids: title:exposomic determinants in heart failure among older adults mechanistic links clinical evidence and future perspectives

title: Uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single-cell analysis.

top_author.name: Laura P. M. H. de Rooij

key_authors.name: Laura P. M. H. de Rooij

abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) are critical regulators of vascular function and exhibit tissue-specialized roles. During aging, these cells become dysfunctional, resulting in increased susceptibility to cardiovascular disease. Although single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive endothelial heterogeneity, a comprehensive atlas of human EC transcriptomes over the course of the adult human lifespan has been lacking. Here, we present the Human Aging Endothelial Cell Atlas (HAECA), a harmonized single-cell transcriptomic compendium of over 375,000 ECs from 12 human tissues throughout adulthood. We identified age-associated transcriptional shifts, including a decline in angiogenic gene expression in venous ECs and widespread alterations in extracellular matrix and mechanotransduction-associated signatures. Furthermore, we uncovered a p21-linked transcriptional program in ECs, which we linked to cellular senescence in both in vitro and in vivo models. Together, our study provides a high-resolution transcriptomic reference of the human endothelium across tissues and age.
ids: title:uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single cell analysis

title: Advances in Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy. XI: Sotatercept in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
abstract: Sotatercept is a groundbreaking new treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The disease-modifying drug is a recombinant fusion protein that consists of the extracellular domain of the activin receptor 2A linked to the Fc fragment of human immunoglobulin G1. Sotatercept potently traps activins and growth differentiation factors to inhibit transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling through its activin receptor 2A/2B pathway, thereby restoring the neutral balance between pro-proliferative and antiproliferative signaling in PAH and causing a striking reversal of the disease's pathologic consequences. This article had the following objectives: (1) describe the parallel TGF-β signaling pathways and their opposing effects on pulmonary artery endothelial and smooth muscle cell quiescence and proliferation; (2) discuss the mechanisms by which sotatercept differentially affects TGF-β signaling to inhibit and reverse aberrant vascular proliferation and facilitate cellular quiescence; (3) review the preclinical evidence indicating that sotatercept has favorable actions in experimental models of PAH; (4) examine the findings of major clinical trials and their substudies demonstrating that sotatercept exerts temporally durable benefits on pulmonary and right ventricular hemodynamics, clinical symptoms, exercise tolerance, quality of life, and mortality in patients with long-standing, high-risk, and newly identified PAH; (5) assess recent findings indicating that sotatercept produces salutary actions in patients with precapillary and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension resulting from heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; and lastly, (6) comment on the adverse effects of sotatercept and its potential anesthetic implications.
ids: title:advances in cardiovascular pharmacotherapy xi sotatercept in pulmonary arterial hypertension

title: Systemic Inflammation and Adverse Heart Failure Outcomes: Insights From the Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: The association between systemic inflammation (SI) and outcomes among patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) is uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association between SI and clinical and economic outcomes among individuals with HFpEF/HFmrEF. We identified Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) testing from 2008 to 2022. We classified Veterans as with SI (hsCRP 2-10 mg/L) and without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L). The primary outcome was the 3-component major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) outcome of death, HF hospitalization, and HF-related emergency department encounters. Additional outcomes included acute care utilization and costs. We evaluated the adjusted associations between SI and clinical outcomes, acute care utilization, and costs via Cox regression, negative binomial regression, and gamma regression, respectively. We identified 49,986 Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient hsCRP levels. We compared 8,696 (17.4%) Veterans without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L) and 25,352 (50.7%) Veterans with SI (hsCRP ≥2 mg/L and ≤10 mg/L Over a median follow-up of 3.4 years (IQR: 1.8-5.8), MACE incidence was 15.1/100 patient-years (95% CI: 14.9-15.4) among those with SI vs 11.8/100 patient-years (95% CI: 11.4-12.1) among those without SI (P < 0.001). After adjustment, SI was associated with increased MACE (HR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.24-1.33). SI was also associated with increased all-cause hospitalizations (incidence rate ratio: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.137-1.246) and $9,112 (95% CI: $6,135-$12,089) in additional per-patient costs over 1 year. Among Veterans with HFmrEF/HFpEF, SI is associated with increased adverse clinical outcomes and higher costs.
ids: title:systemic inflammation and adverse heart failure outcomes insights from the veterans affairs health care system

title: Platelet-macrophage crosstalk in cardiac inflammation and remodeling.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
abstract: Cardiac injury and chronic heart disease are increasingly recognized as multicellular processes driven by dynamic interactions between immune and thrombotic signaling networks. Although platelets and macrophages have been extensively studied individually, the molecular mechanisms through which their reciprocal interactions regulate cardiac inflammation and remodeling remain incompletely defined. A comprehensive understanding of this cellular crosstalk is needed to define the signaling pathways that couple acute injury responses to chronic maladaptive remodeling. Among these interactions, platelet-macrophage crosstalk has emerged as an important regulator of inflammatory responses and tissue remodeling within the injured myocardium. Beyond their traditional roles in hemostasis and innate immunity, platelets communicate with macrophages through adhesion molecules, soluble mediators, and extracellular vesicles, thereby modulating macrophage activation and functional reprogramming. Platelet-derived mediators, including P-selectin, CD40L, PF4 (CXCL4), CCL5, and platelet-derived extracellular vesicles, modulate macrophage inflammatory signaling, cytokine production, redox balance, metabolic reprogramming, and pro-fibrotic responses relevant to cardiac remodeling. During acute myocardial injury, these interactions facilitate immune-cell recruitment, efferocytosis, and tissue repair, whereas persistent platelet-macrophage communication promotes chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and progression to heart failure. This review summarizes current molecular insights into platelet-macrophage interactions, focusing on receptor-mediated signaling, extracellular vesicle cargo transfer, immunometabolic regulation, and redox-dependent pathways. We also discuss emerging evidence linking this axis to trained immunity and inflammatory memory and highlight potential molecular targets for modulating maladaptive immune remodeling in cardiovascular disease.
ids: title:platelet macrophage crosstalk in cardiac inflammation and remodeling

title: The triad of vascular ageing: Cellular senescence, inflammaging, and epigenetic remodelling in atherosclerosis.
abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading global cause of the cardiovascular mortality burden, yet traditional lipid-centric models fail to explain the residual cardiovascular risk observed in older populations. This review, synthesising contemporary literature from 2020 onwards alongside foundational studies, explores the paradigm shift towards the 'geroscience hypothesis', positing that intrinsic biological ageing of the vascular wall is a potent amplifier and primary driver of atherogenesis acting in synergy with circulating lipids. We delineate a pathogenic triad: cellular senescence, systemic inflammaging, and epigenetic dysregulation. At the cellular level, mechanical and metabolic stressors force endothelial and vascular smooth muscle cells into a usually stable senescent state, triggering the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype. Immunologically, ASCVD in the elderly is driven by metabolically exhausted macrophages, the emergence of clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential, and cytotoxic memory T cells. Crucially, metabolic stressors such as hyperglycaemia induce long-lasting alterations to the chromatin landscape of haematopoietic stem cells, establishing 'trained immunity' and a persistent pro-inflammatory metabolic memory. These processes are deeply governed by an altered epigenetic landscape, including the loss of protective sirtuins and aberrant RNA methylation, which dynamically accelerate biological clocks like GrimAge. Clinically, vascular ageing trajectories are highly sexually dimorphic and heavily influenced by midlife metabolic clustering and endocrine shifts and murine models suggest highly sexually dimorphic plaque immunophenotypes. Finally, we evaluate the translational frontier of precision senotherapeutics. We contrast senomorphics, such as repurposed metformin and natural polyphenols that suppress the SASP, with targeted senolytics. Emerging nanotechnology-including in vivo CAR-T lipid nanoparticles and responsive peptide nanoassemblies-offers preclinical proof-of-concept strategies to selectively clear senescent cells without systemic toxicity. Ultimately, mitigating ASCVD requires moving beyond lipid management to integratively target the biological clock of the artery.
ids: title:the triad of vascular ageing cellular senescence inflammaging and epigenetic remodelling in atherosclerosis

title: Lithium-Doped Hydroxyapatite Nanowires Rejuvenate Senescent Macrophages Via the Lysosome-Dependent Ferroptosis Axis to Promote Aged Bone Regeneration.
abstract: Senescent bone repair remains a formidable clinical challenge without an entirely satisfactory strategy. Emerging evidence has identified macrophage senescence as a critical determinant of impaired bone healing in the aged skeleton, and precisely reversing macrophage senescence has therefore emerged as a highly promising therapeutic approach. In this study, guided by multi-omics features of senescent macrophages, we develop lithium-doped hydroxyapatite nanowires (Li-nHAP) and demonstrate that Li-nHAP effectively alleviates macrophage senescence and subsequently enhances the osteogenic differentiation of aged bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Mechanistically, we identify the lysosome-dependent ferroptosis axis as a previously unrecognized target mediating the anti-senescent effects of Li-nHAP in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Specifically, Li-nHAP re-establishes lysosomal homeostasis, including restoring acidity, preserving membrane integrity, maintaining iron storage, and enhancing hydrolytic activity, thereby suppressing ferroptosis and ultimately reversing macrophage senescence. In vivo studies further validate that Li-nHAP significantly alleviates macrophage ferroptosis and senescence, reduces local iron accumulation, and accelerates bone regeneration in an aged mandibular defect model. Collectively, these findings establish Li-nHAP as a novel osteo-immunomodulatory biomaterial that offers a promising strategy for the repair of age-related bone defects.
ids: title:lithium doped hydroxyapatite nanowires rejuvenate senescent macrophages via the lysosome dependent ferroptosis axis to promote aged bone regeneration

title: SPP1⁺ macrophage-derived WNT5A contributes to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade. Methods Bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic data were integrated with clinical immunotherapy cohorts. Weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, survival meta‑analysis, and tissue enrichment scoring identified high‑risk cell subpopulations. Cell‑cell communication, virtual gene knockout, and spatial deconvolution were used to predict ligand‑receptor interactions and colocalization. Multiplex immunohistochemistry of clinical specimens validated spatial relationships. In vitro, MMP11-overexpressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1-overexpressing macrophages (Macs) were generated, and a macrophage-CAF co‑culture system was constructed. Migration, contractility, extracellular matrix deposition, and YAP/INHBA pathway activation was measured. In vivo, a murine tumor model was established and evaluated using in vivo imaging, flow cytometry, atomic force microscopy assay, HE, masson staining, and multiplexed IHC staining. Results MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic CAF (MMP11⁺ myCAF) was identified as a high-risk CAF subset enriched in primary tumor and metastatic lesions, characterized by elevated expression of matrix-remodeling and contractile genes, including MMP11, ACTA2, and TAGLN. Increased abundance of MMP11⁺ myCAF was associated with advanced tumor stage, metastasis, poor overall survival, and reduced benefit from immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Spatial transcriptomic deconvolution and multiplex immunohistochemistry revealed that MMP11⁺ myCAFs spatially co-localized with SPP1⁺ Mac, a pro-tumor myeloid population enriched in malignant and metastatic LUAD tissues. Ligand-receptor and downstream target analyses identified WNT5A as a key macrophage-derived mediator linking SPP1⁺ Mac to MMP11⁺ myCAF activation. Mechanistically, SPP1⁺ Mac exhibited activation of NFKB2/RELB-associated transcriptional programs, and SPP1 overexpression increased Nfkb2, Relb, and WNT5A protein levels in macrophages. WNT5A stimulation promoted YAP/INHBA-associated signaling in CAFs, enhancing CAF migration, contractility and extracellular matrix deposition. In animal models, activation of WNT5A signaling impaired the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 blockade, reduced intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and increased MMP11⁺ CAF-associated collagen deposition and tissue stiffness. Conclusions SPP1⁺ Mac-derived WNT5A may contribute to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy to overcome ICB resistance.
ids: title:spp1 macrophage derived wnt5a contributes to mmp11 mycaf mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma

title: Whole genome sequencing identifies genetic variants associated with senescence-accelerated phenotype of OXYS rats.
abstract: Age is the primary risk factor for age-related diseases, the early onset of which manifests as premature aging, whereas delayed development forms the basis for healthy aging and longevity. Adverse genetic variants contribute to premature aging and its diverse manifestations, including increased multimorbidity. Identifying the genetic underpinnings of premature aging and developing preventive approaches are essential to extending the human healthspan, which requires fundamental research using animal models. In this study, we performed whole-genome sequencing (coverage depth >25×) of OXYS rats - a unique model of premature aging characterized by the early onset of geriatric disorders, including cataracts, AMD-like retinopathy, Alzheimer's disease-like pathology, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy - using the parental Wistar/Icgn rat strain as a control. The screening for single-nucleotide variants (SNVs), short insertions/deletions (indels), and copy number variations (CNVs) and comparative genomic analysis revealed genetic variants unique to OXYS rats that are absent in other rat strains. Specifically, we identified a large deletion in the Fat1 enhancer, deletions in the promoter regions of Abcf1 and Gsta6, and missense variants in Cic, Akap6, Nqo2, Cerkl, Bfsp1, and Cmya5 that lead to amino acid substitutions in highly conserved protein regions. Bioinformatic analysis suggested that these variants may contribute to the key features of premature aging in OXYS rats. Notably, deletions in the Fat1 enhancer and Gsta6 promoter, alongside missense substitutions in Cic, Akap6, and Nqo2, may drive early neurodegeneration and cognitive deficits by disrupting neurogenesis, reducing neuronal survival, and impairing antioxidant defense. The deletion in the Abcf1 promoter and the missense variants in Cerkl may induce retinopathy features by disrupting retinal homeostasis and weakening the protection of photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells against oxidative stress and apoptosis. Furthermore, the missense substitution in Bfsp1 likely contributes to early cataract development by reducing the stability of lens intermediate filaments. Finally, missense variants in Cmya5 and Akap6 may promote sarcopenia and cardiomyopathy via the destabilization of myofibrils in skeletal muscles and cardiomyocytes (Cmya5) and through impaired skeletal muscle regeneration and structural disorganization of cardiomyocytes (Akap6).
ids: title:whole genome sequencing identifies genetic variants associated with senescence accelerated phenotype of oxys rats

title: Macrophage-Derived Glycoprotein Nonmetastatic Melanoma Protein B Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Promoting Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-Independent Angiogenesis.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Background Pressure overload-induced heart failure involves maladaptive cardiac remodeling and inadequate angiogenesis. The limitations of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)-based therapies underscore the need to identify alternative angiogenic pathways. GPNMB (glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B) is a macrophage-secreted protein implicated in tissue repair, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and its potential to modulate angiogenesis remain unknown. Methods Myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout and control mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction. Cardiac function, remodeling, and capillary density were assessed. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptomic changes. In vitro, human endothelial cells were treated with recombinant GPNMB to assess proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and to dissect the underlying signaling pathways. The therapeutic potential of Gpnmb overexpression was evaluated using AAV9 vectors. Results Myeloid Gpnmb deletion exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and capillary rarefaction. Single-cell sequencing revealed a reduced capillary endothelial cell population and pathway enrichment indicative of endothelial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming in myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout hearts. Mechanistically, GPNMB directly promoted endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation by activating the mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, independently of VEGF signaling. Cardiac-specific Gpnmb overexpression rescued angiogenesis, improved cardiac function, and attenuated pathological remodeling after transverse aortic constriction. Conclusions Macrophage-derived GPNMB is a critical regulator of cardiac adaptation to pressure overload. It promotes a VEGF-independent angiogenic program probably via the CD44/mTOR axis, as supported by in vitro mechanistic studies. GPNMB represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure characterized by microvascular rarefaction.
ids: title:macrophage derived glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein b attenuates cardiac dysfunction by promoting vascular endothelial growth factor independent angiogenesis

title: Lactylation modification: a new bridge connecting macrophage metabolism and pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a multifactorial, progressive disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and right heart failure, representing a substantial global health burden. Dysregulated interactions among multiple cell types within the pulmonary vascular microenvironment, particularly macrophage polarization imbalance with a predominant transition toward the M2 phenotype, play a critical role in driving pro-fibrotic and pro-remodeling processes in PH. Lactylation, a novel post-translational modification that covalently links lactate to lysine residues, translates glycolytic metabolic signals into persistent epigenetic changes. Recent advances have identified lactylation on histones (e.g., H3K18la), non-histone proteins, and mitochondrial proteins, revealing new layers of regulatory complexity. Elucidating the role of lactylation, particularly its impact on macrophage polarization and vascular cell function, may offer novel insights into the pathogenesis of PH and identify potential therapeutic targets. KEY POINTS: • Macrophage polarization imbalance (predominant M2 phenotype) is a critical driver of pulmonary vascular remodeling in pulmonary hypertension (PH), and lactylation serves as a novel metabolic-epigenetic bridge linking macrophage metabolic reprogramming and phenotypic switching. • Lactylation modifications occur extensively on histones, non-histone proteins, and mitochondrial proteins in PH, regulating fibrosis-related pathways, arginine metabolism signaling, and the dysfunction of pulmonary vascular cells. • Targeting lactylation and lactate metabolism represents a promising therapeutic strategy for PH, supported by our previous studies on M2 macrophage polarization and ongoing lactylomic research.
ids: title:lactylation modification a new bridge connecting macrophage metabolism and pulmonary hypertension

title: Enzymatic extracellular matrix remodeling in ex vivo slices of aged myocardium
abstract: Cardiac aging is accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and increased myocardial stiffness, which may contribute to age-associated functional decline. However, whether direct remodeling of the aged cardiac ECM can modify myocardial mechanics and function remains poorly understood. Here, we established an ex vivo living myocardial slice platform to investigate whether enzymatic remodeling of the aged ECM can alter myocardial structure, mechanics, and function. Left ventricular myocardial slices (LMS) from young and aged mice were maintained under static stretch for 48 hours using a custom 3D-printed culture setup. Aged slices were treated with collagenase and subsequently characterized using quantitative imaging, tensile testing, contractility measurements, and transcriptomic analysis. Aged myocardium exhibited increased collagen and fibronectin abundance, altered collagen network architecture, and increased stiffness compared with young tissue. Collagenase treatment reduced collagen and network complexity and reduced myocardial stiffness toward young tissue values without compromising ultimate tensile stress. Despite these structural and biomechanical changes, age-associated differences in myocardial contractility remained comparable across groups. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that treated aged tissue largely retained its age-associated molecular phenotype, despite pathway-level shifts involving metabolism, cardiac function, and inflammatory responses. These findings demonstrate that enzymatic ECM remodeling can modify the aged myocardial mechanical environment while selected functional and transcriptional features of aging persist over 48 hours. The LMS platform provides a controllable ex vivo tissue-level approach for investigating ECM contributions during cardiac aging and evaluating strategies for ECM engineering. Statement of significance Cardiac aging is accompanied by progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and tissue stiffening, which are associated with impaired cardiac function. However, studying how these age-related changes influence living myocardium requires models that balance physiological complexity and experimental control. This study combines living myocardial slice culture with controlled enzymatic ECM remodeling to examine aged tissue responses within the native myocardial environment. Collagenase treatment reduced tensile modulus and altered collagen network organization, while selected functional and transcriptional features of aging persisted over 48 hours. These findings demonstrate the utility of living myocardial slices for evaluating matrix-targeted interventions and highlight the importance of assessing biological responses alongside changes in ECM structure and tissue mechanics.
ids: title:enzymatic extracellular matrix remodeling in ex vivo slices of aged myocardium

title: SGLT-2 inhibitor dapagliflozin improves left ventricular diastolic function and reduces circulating inflammatory markers in HFpEF patients: a retrospective cohort study.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: This study sought to evaluate the efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor Dapagliflozin in ameliorating left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF) and attenuating systemic inflammatory biomarkers in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). A total of 114 patients diagnosed with HFpEF were retrospectively enrolled and allocated into either the SGLT-2 inhibitor group (Dapagliflozin combined with standard guideline-directed therapy; n = 58) or the Control group (standard guideline-directed therapy alone; n = 56). Echocardiographic parameters at baseline and 6-month follow-up were measured, including early diastolic transmitral flow velocity/early diastolic mitral annular velocity ratio (E/e') and left atrial volume index (LAVI). Circulating inflammatory markers comprising high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) were examined. In addition, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels and Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ) scores were collected for functional and symptomatic assessments. After six months of treatment, the SGLT-2 inhibitor group exhibited significant improvements in cardiac diastolic parameters. E/e' ratio decreased significantly from 14.8 ± 3.2 to 12.1 ± 2.7 (P < 0.001), and LAVI decreased from 38.6 ± 8.4 to 34.2 ± 7.1 mL/m2 (P = 0.003). Consistently, systemic inflammation was markedly alleviated. hs-CRP decreased from 4.82 ± 1.73 to 2.94 ± 1.28 mg/L (P < 0.001), IL-6 decreased from 8.46 ± 2.91 to 5.73 ± 2.14 pg/mL (P = 0.002), and TNF-α decreased from 12.8 ± 4.6 to 9.4 ± 3.8 pg/mL (P = 0.011). Moreover, NT-proBNP levels in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group exhibited a substantial 28.4% reduction, which was significantly greater than the 8.7% reduction observed in the Control group (P = 0.004). There was also a striking reduction in MLHFQ scores in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group (average reduction: -8.6 ± 4.2 points, P < 0.001), demonstrating significant symptomatic improvement. SGLT-2 inhibitor Dapagliflozin effectively improved LVDF and reduced systemic inflammatory burden in patients with HFpEF. These findings support the role of Dapagliflozin as a promising disease-modifying therapeutic agent for HFpEF.
ids: title:sglt 2 inhibitor dapagliflozin improves left ventricular diastolic function and reduces circulating inflammatory markers in hfpef patients a retrospective cohort study

title: Mapping cellular senescence in heart failure: knowledge evolution, mechanistic modules, and senotherapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Cellular senescence is increasingly recognized as a mechanistic link between cardiovascular ageing, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, and heart failure (HF) progression. However, the knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and translational frontiers of senescence research in HF remain incompletely mapped. This study mapped the global research landscape of cellular senescence in HF from 2005 to 2025 by integrating dual-database bibliometric analysis with BERTopic-based semantic topic modelling. English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After field verification, standardization, and deduplication, 479 publications were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, SCImago Graphica, Pajek, Python, and Microsoft Excel were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses. PubMedBERT-based embeddings and BERTopic were applied to identify latent semantic themes from titles, abstracts, and keywords. Publications increased rapidly after 2020, with 336 papers published between 2020 and 2025, accounting for 70.1% of the corpus. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with the United States showing higher collaboration strength and accumulated citation counts within the analysed dataset. Co-citation analysis identified foundational studies in senescence biology, senolytics, cardiovascular ageing, and HF remodelling. Keyword evolution showed a shift from oxidative stress, cardiac stem/progenitor cell senescence, and vascular cell senescence toward inflammation, metabolic remodelling, biomarkers, HF phenotypes, and senotherapeutics. BERTopic identified 17 substantive topics, with Cardiac and Cardiovascular Aging as the largest theme, followed by Cardiac Fibrosis and Fibroblast Activation, SASP-related Cardiovascular Senescence, Cardiac Regeneration, and Doxorubicin Cardiotoxicity. Bibliometric and semantic analyses indicate growing research interest in cell-type-specific senescence, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, HF phenotype heterogeneity, biomarkers, and senotherapeutics. These findings highlight opportunities for integrating mechanistic research with clinical investigation. Future studies should prioritize cell-specific senescence atlases, multidimensional biomarkers, comorbidity-aware HF stratification, and cautious evaluation of senotherapeutics in HF subgroups with evidence of senescence-associated pathology.
ids: title:mapping cellular senescence in heart failure knowledge evolution mechanistic modules and senotherapeutic opportunities

title: Particulate Matter Exposure and Accelerated Cardiovascular Aging: Mechanistic Evidence, Biomarker Integration, and the PACA Framework.
abstract: Particulate matter exposure, particularly PM2.5 and ultrafine particles, is a well-established risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity. However, whether pollution-associated cardiovascular abnormalities represent transient toxicity, cumulative injury, developmental programming, aging-like phenotypes, or a genuine alteration in the trajectory of cardiovascular aging remains unresolved. Here, we propose the Pollution-Accelerated Cardiovascular Aging (PACA) framework as a conceptual, hypothesis-generating approach for interpreting this distinction. Rather than proposing new molecular mechanisms, we integrate established pathways, including mitochondrial and redox dysfunction, genomic and epigenetic alterations, cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype signaling, impaired proteostasis, endothelial dysfunction, and autonomic dysregulation within an explicit evidentiary framework. We also consider the pulmonary neural cardiac axis as a potential route through which pulmonary sensory activation may influence autonomic regulation, calcium handling, and cardiac electrophysiological function. To distinguish exposure-associated toxicity from evidence consistent with altered cardiovascular aging, we introduce a Temporal-Evidence Matrix that integrates exposure kinetics, life-course timing, persistence and recovery after exposure cessation, exposure response relationships, and longitudinal change relative to age-referenced comparators. Persistence, incomplete recovery, or cumulative loss of cardiovascular reserve support chronic or sustained injury but do not independently establish accelerated aging. Stronger evidence for PACA requires repeated longitudinal demonstration that particulate exposure is associated with a greater rate or altered trajectory of aging-related cardiovascular or biological change than expected from chronological aging. Finally, we propose a tiered biomarker framework that separates candidate biological-aging integrators from mechanistic stress and injury indicators and contextual inflammatory markers, while treating vascular and cardiac functional or imaging measures as complementary cardiovascular phenotypes. The principal contribution of PACA is therefore evidentiary rather than mechanistic, providing a structured approach for testing whether particulate exposure is associated with cardiovascular toxicity alone or with an altered cardiovascular-aging trajectory.
ids: title:particulate matter exposure and accelerated cardiovascular aging mechanistic evidence biomarker integration and the paca framework

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled deep clinical phenotyping in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: from patient subtypes to precision care.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
keywords: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a clinical syndrome defined by shared manifestations but produced by diverse combinations of cardiometabolic, vascular, inflammatory, renal, pulmonary, atrial, skeletal-muscle, and aging-related mechanisms. This heterogeneity limits the value of classifications based only on left ventricular ejection fraction and helps explain why many mechanistically plausible interventions have produced neutral average results. Deep phenotyping can move the field from descriptive heterogeneity toward biologically coherent and clinically actionable subtypes by integrating clinical trajectories, advanced imaging, exercise and invasive hemodynamics, circulating biomarkers, multiomics, and digital physiology. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers methods to combine these high-dimensional data, but statistical clusters should not be equated with disease endotypes. A useful subtype must be reproducible across cohorts, anchored to plausible biology, associated with a distinct clinical course, and able to improve diagnosis, therapeutic selection, or clinical-trial design. This Review examines the translational continuum from experimental HFpEF models to human patient subtypes, summarizes the main deep-phenotyping domains and AI approaches, and proposes seven clinically interpretable subtype families: cardiometabolic-inflammatory, hypertensive-vascular aging, atrial myopathy, pulmonary vascular-right ventricular, cardiorenal-congestive, peripheral-frailty, and specific etiologic phenocopies. Current evidence supports a layered treatment strategy in which broadly effective therapies, particularly sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, are combined with phenotype-directed management of obesity, diabetes, mineralocorticoid receptor activation, atrial fibrillation, congestion, pulmonary vascular disease, and physical deconditioning. The central next step is prospective validation of dynamic subtype assignments in external populations and phenotype-enriched trials. Phenogroup labels should therefore be regarded as pragmatic, transitional proxies for dominant mechanisms when those mechanisms cannot yet be measured directly at the individual-patient level; their value lies in improving decisions while the field moves toward fully individualized mechanism-based treatment. Deep phenotyping will be clinically valuable only when it changes a decision and improves an outcome, rather than merely increasing descriptive complexity.
ids: title:artificial intelligence enabled deep clinical phenotyping in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction from patient subtypes to precision care

title: An α1D-adrenergic receptor vaccine protects against HFpEF in mice.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a global clinical challenge with high mortality and restricted therapeutic options. Persistent sympathetic nervous system (SNS) overactivation, systemic metabolic dysregulation, and chronic inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF pathogenesis. We developed ADRQβ-004, a novel therapeutic vaccine targeting α1D-adrenergic receptor (α1D-AR), to evaluate its potential in mitigating HFpEF. A "two-hit" HFpEF mouse model was established in 6-week-old male ApoE-/- mice via high-fat diet and Nω- nitro-L-arginine methyl ester administration for 17 weeks. Mice were subcutaneously immunized with five doses of ADRQβ-004. We comprehensively assessed blood pressure, glucose/lipid metabolism, diastolic function, and cardiac remodeling. Pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) was specifically analyzed via histology, RNA-seq, and biochemical assays. Furthermore, a monoclonal antibody (ADR-004) was employed in an adipocyte-cardiomyocyte co-culture system to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. ADRQβ-004 elicited high and sustained titer of specific antibody, demonstrating robust immunogenicity. Vaccination significantly improved glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles in HFpEF mice. Morphological and functional analyses revealed that ADRQβ-004 markedly attenuated left ventricular remodeling, diastolic dysfunction, and myocardial mitochondrial impairment. Notably, the vaccine suppressed PAT inflammation and metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, blockade of α1D-AR via ADR-004 activated the PPARβ/AMPK/PGC1-α signaling pathway in adipocytes, which subsequently modulated adipocyte-cardiomyocyte crosstalk, leading to enhanced myocardial mitochondrial function and improved HFpEF phenotypes. The ADRQβ-004 vaccine ameliorates HFpEF by modulating adipocyte-cardiomyocyte crosstalk through the PPARβ/AMPK/PGC1-α pathway. These findings suggest that ADRQβ-004 may serve as a promising immunomodulatory strategy for HFpEF research.
ids: title:an 1d adrenergic receptor vaccine protects against hfpef in mice

title: Depression and Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: An Inflammatory Perspective.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: Depression is a common comorbidity in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), suggesting potential epidemiological and pathophysiological connections between these two age-related chronic diseases. Extensive clinical evidence demonstrates that depression is closely associated with both the incidence and prognosis of HFpEF. It is currently believed that depression may contribute to the pathogenesis of HFpEF through various interconnected mechanisms, including intestinal dysfunction, endothelial dysfunction, disturbances in fat and energy metabolism, autonomic nervous system dysfunction, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis imbalance, and sex differences. Both conditions often share common comorbidities and genetic predispositions. Notably, inflammation is implicated in all these mechanisms and processes, playing a key role at different stages and facilitating the interaction between the two diseases during their onset and progression. However, the connections between depression and HFpEF have not yet been systematically and thoroughly elucidated. This review aims to comprehensively summarize the associations between depression and HFpEF, focusing particularly on elucidating their interplay in pathogenesis from an inflammation perspective, with special emphasis on the adverse effects of depression on the development of HFpEF. Additionally, we evaluate the management approaches for patients with comorbid depression and HFpEF, which include both pharmacological and nonpharmacological treatments, highlighting that personalized and integrated interventions may offer significant benefits. The review underscores the importance of increased attention and early identification of patients with comorbid depression and HFpEF and is expected to provide valuable insights and guidance for the clinical management of this significant patient population.
ids: title:depression and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction an inflammatory perspective

title: METTL14-Mediated m6A Methylation Preserves Cardiomyocyte Homeostasis and Attenuates Progeria-Associated Cardiac Remodeling.
abstract: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) is a rare premature aging disorder most commonly caused by a de novo synonymous mutation (c.1824C>T) in the LMNA gene. This mutation activates aberrant splicing of prelamin A, leading to the production and accumulation of progerin, which drives accelerated aging, with patients predominantly succumbing to cardiovascular disease. However, while cardiac pathologies are well documented, the cell-autonomous contribution of cardiomyocytes to HGPS-associated cardiac remodeling remains poorly understood. Here, we generated a cardiomyocyte-specific progerin-expressing mouse model (Myh6-Cre; Lmnafl/fl) and found that selective progerin expression in cardiomyocytes was sufficient to recapitulate key cardiac features of HGPS, including myocardial fibrosis, cardiac hypertrophy, and progressive functional decline. Mechanistically, progerin-expressing hearts exhibited a marked reduction in the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) writer components METTL3/14, and knockdown of Mettl3/14 in primary cardiomyocytes decreased the expression of calcium-handling transcript (Casq2), while elevating senescence-related (Cdkn1a and Cdkn2a) and pro-inflammatory transcripts (Ifna and Ifnb). Importantly, cardiomyocyte-targeted restoration of METTL14 partially ameliorated pathological cardiac remodeling and dysfunction in progeroid mice. Together, the data identify METTL14-dependent m6A methylation as a critical regulator of cardiomyocyte integrity during progeria-associated cardiac remodeling. Restoration of cardiac m6A writer activity may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for laminopathy-related cardiovascular aging.
ids: title:mettl14 mediated m6a methylation preserves cardiomyocyte homeostasis and attenuates progeria associated cardiac remodeling

title: Proteomic and β-hydroxybutyrylation Landscapes Reveal AMPKα2-Associated Modulation in HUCMSC-Derived Exosome-Mediated Amelioration of Cardiac Aging.
abstract: Cardiac aging is characterized by progressive functional decline and metabolic remodeling. We previously found that lysine β-hydroxybutyrylation (Kbhb) is altered in wild-type (WT) aged and AMP-activated protein kinase alpha 2 (AMPKα2)-knockout (AK) young hearts, but whether this landscape can be reversed therapeutically remains unknown. We evaluated the therapeutic potential of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cell-derived exosomes (hUCMSC-exos) in WT and AK aged mice, using young and aged untreated cohorts as controls. Quantitative proteomics across six experimental groups identified 1,755 Kbhb sites on 652 proteins, mapping the dynamic cardiac Kbhb landscape under aging, AMPKα2 deficiency, and exosome intervention. In wild-type aged (WTA) mice, hUCMSC-exos improved systolic and diastolic function, enhanced grip strength, reduced fibrosis, and restored ATP levels, accompanied by predominant downregulation of Kbhb on enzymes of glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, fatty acid oxidation, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation. In AMPKα2-knockout aged (AKA) mice, exosomes partially improved mitochondrial ultrastructure and diastolic indices but did not rescue systolic function or fibrosis. Site-level analysis revealed that exosomes selectively normalized Kbhb sites elevated during aging, whereas AMPKα2 deficiency caused nonselective global depletion. The candidate AMPKα2-SIRT3 pathway, supported by SIRT5, may underlie this Kbhb reprogramming. We validated carnitine acetyltransferase (CRAT) K141bhb as an age-accumulated modification reversed by exosomes in an AMPKα2- associated manner. Molecular modeling indicated that K141bhb neutralizes the positive charge of K141, disrupting the local salt bridge between K141 and E144 and destabilizing the α-helical structure, suggesting that K141bhb may serve as a metabolic brake on CRAT activity. These findings map the cardiac Kbhb landscape and show that hUCMSC-exos ameliorate cardiac aging through AMPKα2- associated Kbhb modulation.
ids: title:proteomic and hydroxybutyrylation landscapes reveal ampk 2 associated modulation in hucmsc derived exosome mediated amelioration of cardiac aging

title: Potential roles for transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which diastolic dysfunction develops against a background of interacting mechanisms: inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired calcium homeostasis, myocardial fibrosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and neurohumoral activation. Effective mechanism-targeted therapies remain limited. Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is a nonselective cation channel expressed in cardiac sensory nerves, vascular endothelial cells, immune cells, and possibly other cardiovascular cell populations. It responds to diverse physical and chemical stimuli and may influence calcium handling, inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, mitophagy, and ferroptosis. Preclinical studies have linked altered TRPV1 expression or activity to myocardial remodeling, impaired relaxation, microvascular dysfunction, and heart failure progression, but direct evidence in HFpEF is still sparse. This review summarizes the biological properties of TRPV1, considers how its signaling might intersect with HFpEF pathophysiology, reviews experimental TRPV1-targeted interventions, and identifies the evidence needed before TRPV1 can be evaluated as a potential therapeutic target.
ids: title:potential roles for transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

title: Novel bioactive compounds in the treatment of osteoporosis: chemistry-driven discovery from preclinical validation to clinical translation.
abstract: Osteoporosis affects an estimated 200 million people worldwide. Fragility fractures of the hip, spine, and wrist carry high mortality and impose a heavy socioeconomic burden. Bisphosphonates, denosumab, selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), teriparatide, abaloparatide, and the recent sclerostin antibody romosozumab have improved clinical outcomes, but unmet needs remain. Long-term antiresorptive use is complicated by atypical femoral fractures and osteonecrosis of the jaw; denosumab discontinuation causes rebound bone loss; romosozumab carries a cardiovascular caution. Persistence on therapy beyond 1 year is low, and no oral osteoanabolic agent has reached the clinic. Against this background, medicinal chemistry is producing a wave of next-line compounds. These include rationally designed small molecules and peptidomimetics targeting the Wnt pathway, calcium-sensing receptor antagonists (calcilytics) intended to mimic pulsatile parathyroid hormone, refined cathepsin K inhibitors, modulators of activin and myostatin signaling, and bone-targeted nanomedicines. Plant-derived scaffolds with anti-osteoporotic activity, particularly icariin, icaritin, genistein, naringin, resveratrol, curcumin, oleanolic acid, psoralen, and berberine, are being optimized chemically to address poor bioavailability. Senolytic combinations and PROTAC-based degraders represent newer modes of action. This review examines the chemistry behind these compounds, their structure-activity relationships, their preclinical pharmacology, and their progress through clinical evaluation. We pay particular attention to the failures (odanacatib, calcilytics, integrin antagonists, Src inhibitors) as well as the successes, because the lessons from attrition shape the chemistry choices that follow. We attempt to identify those chemistry-led strategies that have most reliably accelerated bench-to-bedside translation in bone disease, and those that have not.
ids: title:novel bioactive compounds in the treatment of osteoporosis chemistry driven discovery from preclinical validation to clinical translation

title: MAPK15 induces cardiomyocyte senescence and atrial fibrillation by promoting mitochondrial calcium overload via palmitoylating Mcub at the C91 residue.
abstract: The prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), particularly age-related AF, is increasing rapidly with global aging. Cellular senescence is a key contributing factor to AF, yet the underlying mechanisms driving atrial cardiomyocyte senescence remain elusive. Although MAPK15 has recently been implicated in regulating epithelial cell senescence, its potential role in the heart remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the role of MAPK15 in atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF, and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We investigated the role and underlying mechanisms of MAPK15 in atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF by cardiac-specific overexpression or knockdown of MAPK15, as well as treatment with small-molecule inhibitors. A combination of transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling, co-immunoprecipitation with mass spectrometry, site-directed mutagenesis, patch-clamp recording, optical mapping and intracardiac electrophysiology was employed both in vitro and in vivo. Findings were further validated using human atrial appendage specimens. Results showed that MAPK15 was closely associated with atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF. Overexpression of MAPK15 aggravated senescence and promoted AF. Mechanistically, MAPK15 induced palmitoylation of mitochondrial calcium uniporter dominant negative subunit b (Mcub) at C91, causing its dissociation from the mitochondrial Mcu complex and translocation to the cytoplasm. This impaired inhibition of mitochondrial calcium uptake, leading to calcium overload, ROS overproduction, and cellular senescence. C91S mutation or palmitoylation inhibition (2-BP) reversed these effects. Subsequently, senescent cardiomyocytes showed increased triggered activity, fibrosis, and altered connexin43 distribution, facilitating AF onset. And serological analysis suggested that IL-17a may act as an upstream regulator of MAPK15. Our findings identify MAPK15 as a novel regulator of atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF. MAPK15 promotes mitochondrial calcium overload through palmitoylation of Mcub at C91, highlighting a new mechanistic axis linking mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and arrhythmogenesis. Age-related atrial fibrillation is highly prevalent and frequently associated with adverse cardio- and cerebrovascular events, constituting a significant global public health burden. In this study, we demonstrated at both in vivo and in vitro levels that the MAPK15-Mcub axis promotes atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and senescence-associated AF, which was further validated in atrial appendage tissues from clinical patients, enhancing the clinical translational relevance of our findings. Moreover, we identified circulating IL-17a as a potential upstream activator associated with MAPK15 signaling, suggesting its potential utility in preclinical screening and as an insightful clue for future immunomodulatory strategies. The development of small-molecule agents specially targeting MAPK15 or Mcub in cardiomyocytes may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for treating atrial myocyte senescence and AF.
ids: title:mapk15 induces cardiomyocyte senescence and atrial fibrillation by promoting mitochondrial calcium overload via palmitoylating mcub at the c91 residue

title: Epicardial adipose tissue in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, imaging, and therapeutic modulation.
keyword_hits: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abstract: Obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) often coexist, but the contribution of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) to their overlap remains uncertain. EAT is anatomically contiguous with the myocardium and can undergo inflammatory, profibrotic and metabolic remodeling in obesity. In HFpEF, greater EAT burden is associated with higher filling pressures and findings compatible with external cardiac restraint; in AF, regional peri-atrial fat is associated with abnormal conduction, fibrosis and ablation outcomes. Human EAT experiments demonstrate local profibrotic signaling, while autonomic interventions involving epicardial fat pads provide procedural evidence that does not isolate adipocyte effects. Recent invasive observations in patients with AF also link CT-defined EAT to atrial pressures and obesity-related HFpEF. Exercise, weight loss and metabolic therapies can change measured cardiac fat, although the relevant compartments and responses vary. CT attenuation is not a direct or uniformly directional measure of EAT inflammation. EAT is therefore a measurable phenotype at the HFpEF-AF interface, with stronger local experimental evidence in AF than in HFpEF. Whether changing EAT itself contributes to clinical benefit beyond systemic weight loss or other treatment effects requires longitudinal studies in patients with both conditions.
ids: title:epicardial adipose tissue in obesity related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation mechanisms imaging and therapeutic modulation

title: The AIM2 inflammasome drives age-dependent cardiac dysfunction following ischemia-reperfusion in mice.
abstract: Cardiac aging increases susceptibility to cardiovascular diseases, particularly myocardial infarction. Although evidence suggest association between activation of the AIM2 inflammasome and cardiovascular diseases, its contribution to age-related cardiac complications remains unknown. We investigated the role of the AIM2 inflammasome and the cardiac response to ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury in aged mice. Male wildtype (C57BL/6) and AIM2-deficient (AIM2-/-) mice were subjected to natural aging (21 months), using 3-month-old mice as controls, and human cardiomyocytes (AC16) were stressed by hydrogen peroxide to mimic senescent. AIM2 expression was upregulated in the aged myocardium and senescent AC16 cells, coinciding with increased levels of cleaved caspase-1 (p20), IL-1β, and IL-18. Functional assays in Langendorff-perfused hearts revealed that AIM2 deficiency significantly attenuated post-I/R dysfunction in aged mice, restoring left ventricular developed pressure (LVDP) and pressure derivatives (+dP/dTmax and -dP/dTmin) toward pre-ischemic levels. While AIM2 absence did not alter age-associated hypertrophy, fibrosis, longevity, or senescence markers (p53 and p21), it reduced the baseline pro-inflammatory and pro-pyroptotic profile of the aged heart (IL-1β, IL-18, GSDMD-N, and ASC speck). In vitro, AIM2 activation using Poly(dA:dT) elevated IL-1β, GSDMD-N, ASC speck, and cell death in senescent cells, whereas pharmacological inhibition with A151 prevented these effects. Concurrently, age-dependent AIM2 upregulation was confirmed in human cardiac datasets. Together, these findings suggest that age-dependent AIM2 induction primes a pro-inflammatory cardiac microenvironment, exacerbating post-I/R injury and highlighting this pathway for future investigation in the context of cardiac aging.

title: Selenium alleviates cadmium-induced ovarian fibrosis by inhibiting macrophage senescence in chickens.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a ubiquitous environmental pollutant, and the ovarian fibrosis it induces represents both a critical trigger and a pathological hallmark of female reproductive aging; however, the underlying mechanisms and effective interventions remain poorly defined. The present study demonstrates that dietary selenium (Se) alleviates Cd-induced ovarian fibrosis in chickens. In vivo macrophage depletion experiments revealed that macrophages serve as the key cellular mediators of both Cd-induced ovarian toxicity and the protective effects of Se. In vitro studies showed that Cd induces ferroptotic stress in macrophages, characterized by Fe²⁺ overload and the accumulation of lipid peroxides, which in turn activates the DNA damage response and contributes to cellular senescence. The ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) recapitulated the anti-senescence effects of Se, supporting that ferroptotic stress contributes to macrophage senescence. Transwell co-culture assays further demonstrated that Cd-treated senescent macrophages promoted fibroblast activation, accompanied by increased paracrine secretion of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors, including TGF-β1 and IL-6. Mechanistically, Se restored GPX4 activity and reduced lipid peroxidation, thereby suppressing ferroptotic stress-associated macrophage senescence and SASP secretion; GPX4 knockdown experiments further supported the involvement of GPX4 in these protective effects. Together, these findings indicate that Se mitigates Cd-induced ovarian fibrosis and suggest that GPX4 contributes to its protective effects against ferroptotic stress and macrophage senescence, providing a novel theoretical basis for understanding ovarian fibrosis and reproductive impairment caused by environmental heavy metal exposure.

title: Cellular Senescence as a Core Mechanistic Link between CKD, Cardiac Fibrosis, and Aging.
abstract: CKD and cardiovascular disease frequently coexist and represent a major global health burden. Cellular senescence may connect these disorders through persistent inflammation, fibrosis, and metabolic stress. Senescent cells undergo sustained proliferative arrest and release a pro-inflammatory, pro-fibrotic secretome called the senescence-associated secretory phenotype. In kidney and heart tissue, persistent senescent cells may promote immune-cell infiltration, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix deposition, and tissue stiffening. Human biopsy, cardiac-tissue, urinary-biomarker, circulating-proteomic, and early senolytic data support associations between senescence markers, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular remodelling. However, most causal and interventional evidence still comes from cell-culture and animal models. This review critically evaluates cellular senescence as a plausible cardiorenal-fibrosis mechanism while emphasizing that causality, biomarker specificity, and therapeutic benefit in humans remain to be fully elucidated.
ids: title:cellular senescence as a core mechanistic link between ckd cardiac fibrosis and aging

title: Crystalline silica exposure causes latent biomechanical abnormalities along the cardiopulmonary axis
abstract: Rationale Crystalline silica exposure is a major global health burden linked to chronic lung disease and cardiopulmonary morbidity, but early lung-vascular-cardiac abnormalities preceding overt functional decline are poorly defined. Objectives To determine whether a single crystalline silica exposure produces subclinical abnormalities across the integrated axis of cardiopulmonary response (lung→pulmonary artery→right ventricle) and identify associated sex-dependent physiologic patterns and molecular programs. Methods Male and female mice received a single endotracheal instillation of crystalline silica or vehicle (saline). At 28 days, assessments included voluntary wheel running, diffusion capacity, pulmonary function testing, bronchoalveolar lavage analysis, lung histology and electron microscopy, ex vivo proximal pulmonary artery biomechanics and microstructural second harmonic generation imaging, right ventricular pressure, transthoracic echocardiography, and bulk RNA sequencing of lung and right ventricle. Results Despite recovery of body weight and preserved voluntary exercise, silica-exposed mice demonstrated reduced diffusion capacity, ultrastructural thickening, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier. Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed persistent inflammation with elevated macrophages, lymphocytes, neutrophils, and protein, alongside retained particulate and surfactant-rich debris (silicoproteinosis). Lung mechanics were sex-dependent; females showed a parenchymal-dominant phenotype and males showed increased airway resistance. Elevated pulmonary circulatory pressures caused increased functional stiffness and reduced distensibility of the proximal pulmonary arteries. Right ventricular free wall thickening was noted in females. Lung transcriptomics indicated persistent immune activation and extracellular matrix remodeling, while the right ventricle demonstrated metabolic reprogramming with downregulation of structural and reparative programs. Conclusions A single crystalline silica exposure induces a subclinical, multi-compartment cardiopulmonary phenotype characterized by persistent alveolar-capillary injury, pulmonary vascular stiffening, increased right ventricular afterload, sex-dependent pulmonary mechanics, and divergent organ-level transcriptomic responses.

title: Cellular Senescence and Vascular Ageing in Pulmonary Hypertension: Molecular Mechanisms, Therapeutic Strategies, and Translational Endpoints.
abstract: Increased right ventricular afterload, persistent pulmonary vascular remodelling, and the development of right heart failure are the hallmarks of pulmonary hypertension (PH). In PAH, therapies targeting the prostacyclin, nitric oxide-cyclic guanosine monophosphate, and endothelin pathways improve clinical status and haemodynamics, although established vascular remodelling frequently remains incompletely reversible. This review summarises data suggesting that the residual remodelling load in PH is influenced by vascular ageing, specifically stress-induced premature senescence-like phenotypes in pulmonary vascular wall cells. Endothelial repair failure, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell secretory amplification, extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, senescence-associated secretory phenotype signalling, and mechano-metabolic reprogramming are examined as interconnected processes that attenuate vascular plasticity and consolidate disease progression. Pharmacological strategies discussed include senolytic and senomorphic approaches, activin/TGF-β superfamily modulation exemplified by sotatercept, matrix- and mechanotransduction-directed interventions, and metabolic modulation. Finally, vascular ageing-informed PH studies are proposed to incorporate concordant endpoints that align molecular target engagement with pulmonary vascular mechanics, right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling, right ventricular function, and safety outcomes.
